mutants.name: the-encoder-stops-scrubbing
mutants.//: #86. THE mutation this probe exists for: with the scrub gone, a resolved stream url handed in as a reference goes straight out on the wire. If the byte-scan does not go red here it is scanning nothing.
mutants.find: QString scrubForWire(const QString& s) { return looksLikeCredential(s) ? QString() : s; }
mutants.replace: QString scrubForWire(const QString& s) { return s; }

mutants.name: the-credential-predicate-stops-seeing-urls
mutants.//: #86. The other half of the same rule: the predicate itself. A url is the shape a resolved stream always has.

mutants.name: a-long-token-is-no-longer-a-credential
mutants.//: #86. A bare debrid token or infohash carries no scheme and no query key; the hex-run rule is the only thing that catches one.

mutants.name: one-drift-threshold-instead-of-two
mutants.//: #86. Collapsing the hysteresis to a single threshold is exactly the bug that makes a rate controller oscillate: a drift sitting on the deadband arms and disarms on alternate beacons for ever.
mutants.find: const double threshold = nudging ? cfg.releaseSec : cfg.deadbandSec;

mutants.name: the-deadband-boundary-belongs-to-the-loud-side
mutants.//: #86. Exactly AT the threshold must be 'do nothing'. Flipping the comparison is the classic off-by-a-boundary that only an equality case catches.

mutants.name: the-hard-seek-boundary-moves
mutants.//: #86. The other boundary, in the other direction.

mutants.name: the-nudge-clamp-is-removed
mutants.//: #86. Without the clamp a two-second drift asks for a 6.7% rate change, which is audible even pitch-corrected.
mutants.find: d.speed  = clampd(1.0 - d.drift / cfg.correctionSec, 1.0 - cfg.maxNudge, 1.0 + cfg.maxNudge);

mutants.name: a-hostile-clock-is-trusted
mutants.//: #86. Drop the beacon-age sanity guard and one bad clock reading hard-seeks the whole room.

mutants.name: a-paused-host-is-extrapolated-anyway
mutants.//: #86. A paused host does not advance; treating a stale beacon from one as stale position data seeks the guest away from a stopped picture.
mutants.find: const double target = hostPaused ? hostPos : hostPos + beaconAgeSec;

mutants.name: someone-who-could-not-get-the-film-may-still-pause-it
mutants.//: #86. The arbitration rule: an unresolved participant stays in the room but does not steer it.

mutants.name: a-buffering-hold-outlives-a-user-pause
mutants.//: #86. setHostTransport clearing the hold is what stops a guest recovering from a stall resuming a film the user paused on purpose.
mutants.find: held_ = false;   // a human decision replaces the automatic hold
mutants.replace: // a human decision replaces the automatic hold

mutants.name: keep-going-still-waits
mutants.//: #86. Both buffering policies are the user's answer; collapsing them to one is the guess the issue forbids.

mutants.name: an-unresolved-participant-holds-the-room-up
mutants.//: #86. Someone who never got the film cannot be buffering it; letting their stale flag count pauses everyone else indefinitely.

mutants.name: a-rejoin-becomes-a-second-participant
mutants.//: #86. The same id arriving again is a rejoin, not a new person.

mutants.name: join-in-progress-sends-where-before-what
mutants.//: #86. A guest told the position before the item seeks a player still holding the previous one.

mutants.name: a-seek-request-is-not-clamped
mutants.//: #86. The host arbitrates, which includes refusing a nonsensical position rather than relaying it.

mutants.name: a-malformed-line-ends-the-party
mutants.//: #86. One bad control message must not be fatal; the next beacon repairs anything its loss cost.

mutants.name: the-item-is-not-scrubbed-on-the-way-in
mutants.//: #86. Scrubbing at setItem() means a resolved url is never even HELD, so it cannot reach a log, a record or a later message by some other path.
mutants.find: item_ = shareableRef(ref);   // scrubbed on the way IN as well, so nothing unsafe is ever even held

mutants.name: a-resolved-report-is-always-news
mutants.//: #86. The guard that stops a message loop: a resolved report is a hello, the host answers a hello with the room's item, and the item is what made the guest report. Unconditional, this re-opened the film for ever on live hardware.
mutants.find: if (!me || me->resolved) return false;    // already resolved: saying so again is the loop, not the news

mutants.name: the-indicator-stops-counting-who-is-buffering
mutants.//: #86 room indicator. The buffering badge is a COUNT, and the count is what says whether anybody is buffering at all. With the increment gone the badge never appears, while the notice (built from a separate list) still names the staller: a room that says it is waiting for Sam with nothing on screen saying anybody stalled.

mutants.name: wait-for-everyone-names-nobody
mutants.//: #86 room indicator. Under 'wait for everyone' the notice is the one line that says WHO the film stopped for. Dropped, the indicator shows a badge and a paused film with no name.

mutants.name: keep-going-names-the-staller-too
mutants.//: #86 room indicator. The other half of the same rule: under 'keep going' the film is not waiting, so a name would claim the room is holding for somebody it is not.

mutants.name: an-unresolved-participant-counts-as-buffering
mutants.//: #86 room indicator. Somebody who could not get the film is not watching it, so their stale stall flag holds nobody -- the same rule Room::anyoneBuffering applies to the wait itself.
mutants.find: if (!p.resolved) { ++s.unresolved; continue; }   // not watching, so not stalling anybody

mutants.name: a-paused-player-counts-as-recovered
mutants.//: #448. THE bug, put back: a player the room paused reads as recovered, so every hold the room makes releases itself on the next tick.

mutants.name: one-readiness-threshold-instead-of-two
mutants.//: #448. The hysteresis removed: a guest leaves buffering at the same one second it entered at, so a cache hovering there flaps the room.
mutants.find: return wasBuffering ? cacheAheadSec < cfg.leaveAtSec : cacheAheadSec < cfg.enterBelowSec;

mutants.name: the-leave-bound-moves
mutants.//: #448. Ready at two seconds ahead instead of three.

mutants.name: the-enter-bound-moves
mutants.//: #448. Buffering entered at a second and a half instead of below one.

mutants.name: exactly-three-seconds-is-not-ready
mutants.//: #448. The leave boundary given to the buffering side: 'three seconds or more' becomes 'more than three'.

mutants.name: the-end-of-the-file-is-not-ready
mutants.//: #448. A guest whose cache already holds the rest of the film waits for seconds that do not exist.

mutants.name: an-unreadable-cache-reads-as-empty
mutants.//: #448. mpv not answering is taken as an empty cache, so a file still opening holds the room with no evidence.

mutants.name: a-silent-host-reads-as-an-announced-wait
mutants.//: #448. A host from before the field is treated as having said 'wait', so the guest can never tell it does not know.

mutants.name: the-guest-uses-its-own-setting
mutants.//: #448. The guest's indicator follows its own stall setting instead of the host's.

mutants.name: the-beacon-does-not-carry-the-policy
mutants.//: #448. Only a transport carries the policy, so a live change never reaches a guest until the next pause or seek.
